title: instruction-code heatmap + KV-probe + ndjson exporter for continuous-batching profiling
author: Ravi Patel
release_notes: Adds instruction-code (opcode) heatmaps, a lightweight KV-cache probe that records per-batch prefix hit/miss and cache size snapshots, and an NDJSON exporter for ingestion into perf dashboards. All instrumentation is opt-in via flags.
description: Motivation: production regressions traced to complex interactions between kernel instruction sequences and KV-cache churn in continuous-batching workloads require finer telemetry than existing counters. This PR implements: (1) an instruction-code heatmap collector that buckets cycle counts by opcode id ranges and scheduler stage, (2) a KV-cache probe that emits sampled per-batch metadata (hit/miss ratio, top-key-size distribution, eviction events), (3) batch watermarks that tag scheduler events so we can map kernel time back to logical request boundaries under continuous batching, and (4) an NDJSON exporter (line-delimited JSON) that produces heatmap and probe artifacts compatible with our perf dashboard pipeline. Implementation details: low-overhead per-thread circular buffer guarded by relaxed atomics; sampling.rate and sampling.mode controls to trade fidelity vs overhead; CUDA-path uses device clock sample points when permitted, otherwise uses steady_high_res fallback on host. Exporter emits versioned payloads (heatmap_v1, kvcache_v1). A python microbench runner (bench/micro/instr_heatmap_runner.py) simulates prefix churn and long-lived contexts to validate correlation between opcode hotspots and p99 increases. Tests: unit tests for circular buffer safety, deterministic sampling tests, and an end-to-end perf-canary job that validates exporter schema and ingestion. Safety: feature is disabled by default, can be toggled via runtime flags and operator config; no public API changes. Linked follow-ups: ENG-3178 will add dashboard ingestion wiring and threshold alerts.

incident_references: SUP-901: customer observed scatter in token-level latencies during long-running sessions
observed_perf_notes: In local NVSwitch cluster tests, enabling instr heatmap at 0.5% sampling added ~0.3% CPU and ~0.5ms p99 under 4k concurrent seq. KV-probe captured clear miss storms under synthetic prefix rotation where baseline logs were inconclusive.
